attachments.origin_landmark: inferior border of the rib above, from tubercle to costochondral junction
attachments.insertion_landmark: superior border of the rib below

actions: elevate the ribs (primary inspiratory muscle of quiet and forced breathing)

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population (11 spaces, repeating unit)
functional_compartments.function_note: Fibers run obliquely inferomedially (anterolaterally to posteromedially, 'hands in pockets' direction) from costochondral junction posteriorly to the rib angle, where the layer is replaced by the (thin) external intercostal membrane; consistently inspiratory across all 11 spaces per De Troyer et al.'s regional EMG studies.
functional_compartments.source: De Troyer A, Kirkwood PA, Wilson TA (2005) Physiol Rev 85(2):717-756 -- respiratory action and regional functional differences of the intercostal muscles

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); De Troyer A, Kirkwood PA, Wilson TA (2005) Physiol Rev 85(2):717-756 -- respiratory action and regional functional differences of the intercostal muscles

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: High-frequency linear probe in longitudinal (parasagittal) orientation over the target intercostal space, most reliably at the posterior axillary line where the rib is most superficial; probe tilted to follow the rib's curvature. This is the standard approach for an intercostal nerve block, whose target plane lies just deep to this muscle rather than within its own belly.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: External intercostals form the most superficial of the three intercostal layers, running from the rib tubercle posteriorly to the costochondral junction anteriorly (replaced by the external intercostal membrane medial to that); the nerve block target -- the neurovascular bundle -- lies deep to this muscle, in the plane between the internal and innermost intercostal layers just below the inferior rib margin.
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: Two adjacent hyperechoic rib shadows with the hypoechoic intercostal muscle layers spanning between them; the pleura is seen as a bright sliding line deep to the muscle layers, moving with respiration.
structures_at_risk: pleura and underlying lung (pneumothorax) -- the standard named hazard of any needle advanced into the intercostal space
intercostal vessels running with the nerve in the subcostal groove
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: No motor-point/neural-arborization mapping for this muscle's own belly was found in the literature searched. What is well documented is the ultrasound-guided intercostal nerve block, which targets the neurovascular bundle deep to this muscle (between the internal and innermost intercostal layers) for rib fracture analgesia, post-thoracotomy/thoracoscopy pain, and intercostal neuralgia -- included here because it is the real clinical 'injection approach' relevant to this muscle's neurovascular plane, not a claim of an intramuscular BoNT target.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Kannan A, Srinivasan S (2026) 'Image-Guided Interventions for Intercostal Neuralgia: What the Radiologist Needs to Know', J Med Imaging Radiat Oncol, doi:10.1111/1754-9485.70151 -- review of ultrasound- and CT-guided intercostal nerve block/ablation technique; Ajmal S et al (2024) J Bronchology Interv Pulmonol 31(2):183-187, doi:10.1097/LBR.0000000000000937 -- prospective clinical outcomes of intercostal nerve block at the rib angle
